theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks is the only theme that combines top rank with full eligibility, full breadth, strong trend health (hurst_tag 'trend'), and no crowding. The one validated leg (absolute-trend gate) is supportive, and the momentum/durability legs are coincident but not contradicted. This is a trend-following lean, not a forecast.
theses.dissent: Financials leadership on the TSX often marks late-cycle defensiveness, and the 0.79 unscheduled macro surprise share means headline risk can hit banks hardest via credit/rate channels.

theses.subject: Consumer Staples & Retail
theses.thesis: Eligible, trend-healthy (durability 0.82, hurst 'trend'), full breadth, and roughly flat crowding. It is the second-most durable eligible trend in the state, which fits the gate's drawdown-control logic even if the rank is only 3rd.
theses.dissent: Staples are a defensive laggard bet in risk-on regimes; if AI/tech macro narrative (13 mentions) rotates capital back into growth, staples could bleed relative performance despite trend health.

falsifier.text: XST.TO lags the S&P/TSX composite by 3% before the 20-day check-by date

theses.subject: Technology
theses.thesis: Technology is the only scorable theme that is simultaneously eligible, crowded (z 1.18), and trend-mixed. The crowding flag is explicitly a size-down caution, not a sell, and the mean-reverting candidates elsewhere suggest tech leadership is not confirmed. I frame this as underweight relative to the broad eligible set, not a fade.
theses.dissent: The macro narrative is dominated by AI/tech (13 of 29 themes), so crowding may be self-reinforcing near-term and a size-down could miss an upside leg.

falsifier.text: XIT.TO outperforms the S&P/TSX composite by 3% before the 20-day check-by date

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
